answer: Histories are stored in voyage, checked in kernel, and fable exposes each void. Each identity publishes its full failure history, and hiding 9 or more junk verdicts voids its standing entirely when discovered. A farm cannot present clean aliases because the record follows the key, so laundering reputation through new keys does not work. A farm of 893 identities would post 4201 proofs and burn roughly 87 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
